commits.subject: merge: a Merge pressed after a dependency was squash- or rebase-merged on GitHub merges again; a branch check that finds unreviewed commits files the press's card (L3-github-1, L3-github-3)

fixed.problem:
Reviewer's blocking finding (regression from 2faea88). Setup: A squash- or rebase-merged on GitHub, then Merge pressed on its dependent B before Forerunner's next look. Result: the press was refused with '#B changed after the review: look at the new commits, ...'. The record became head_moved, B's row lost its Merge for good, and a card spoke of commits nobody pushed. At the base the same press merged B.

Root cause:
1. ProjectPullRequests.merge ran the new branch check first (buildsOnGone: A's record was not merged yet).
2. checkBeforeMerge rebuilt B onto main, and settleRecord moved B's record to the head the check pushed.
3. The L3-github-3 head check then compared that head with `listed`, the pull requests read before the rebuild. It called headMovedNow(task, staleHead).
4. keepsOwnChange of the stale head (which still held A's original commit) was false, so the press was refused.

The source changes were reverted to 2faea88 and these tests re-run before the fix was applied again.
fixed.how:
1. packages/runtime/src/daemon/pull-requests.ts, merge(): the head check skips a task whose record's reviewed_head_sha the press's branch check just moved (set rebuiltNow). That check pushed the head and its settleRecord already judged the branch as GitHub had it, so the stale listing is not compared.
2. packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts, ReviewedPrMerge.headMovedNow: before it judges, it reads the pull request again (host.getPullRequest). It returns null when the fresh head is the reviewed commit or the pull request is no longer open. Otherwise it judges keepsOwnChange and headMoved on the fresh head, so the record, the task reason and the card name the real head. This covers a watcher's poll that rebuilt B between the press's read and its check.
It follows the reviewer's sketch: skip, plus a re-read for the other stale-listing case. The skip is deterministic, so GitHub's API lag after a force-push cannot bring back the false refusal. ADR 0111's 2026-11-15 amendment gets a fix-up note. docs/maintainers/runtime.md and the user guide's squash bullet are updated.
fixed.check_in_the_app:
Live check 4, on forerunner-sandbox with the real model, in "You press Merge" mode:
1. Create task A ('Write kite/squash.txt with one line') and task B ('Write kite/squash-day.txt after the squash file', waits for A). Run a session; both are accepted. On the Overview, B's row says 'Merges #A first.'.
2. On GitHub, use 'Squash and merge' on A. Within a few seconds, before Forerunner's next look (under a minute), press Merge on B's row in the app.
Expected: the answer reads 'Merging #B.', never '#B changed after the review'. Within about 10 s B is merged on GitHub. B's pull request shows a force-push (rebuilt onto main) and holds only kite/squash-day.txt. main holds both files, and A's change appears once in main's history.
3. Needs you has no card for B. The Tasks row for B reads 'Merged'. A's row reads 'Merged' after the next look.
4. Repeat with GitHub's 'Rebase and merge' on A: same result.
5. Daemon log: 'dependent pull request rebuilt' for B, then 'merge record ... merged'. There is no 'head_moved' for B.

fixed.problem: Sibling of the blocking finding (validation rule 8). Setup: a commit was pushed to B's branch on GitHub, then A was squash-merged, then Merge was pressed on B before any poll. The press was refused with the right head-moved sentence, but no card was filed. The press's own branch check found the commit, and its changedAfterReview files no card over a record that waited for the click. The L3-github-3 path (headMovedNow with pressed=true) files one card for the same press.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/dependent-branches-merge.test.ts "l3-merge, run L3" > "L3-github-3 fix-up, sibling: a commit pushed to B's branch on GitHub and A squash-merged, Merge pressed on B before any poll: refused at once as changed after the review, nothing merged, one card". It failed at 2faea88 on the card assertion (expected one card, got none).
fixed.how: New BranchCheckOptions { pressed?: boolean } in loop/merge.ts. BranchCheck now takes (task, o?) and checkBranchNow takes (task, o = {}). The press calls checkBranchNow(task, { pressed: true }). DependentBranches.checkBeforeMerge(task, o) passes it to settleRecord(r, pr, pressed) and then to changedAfterReview(task, record, pr, pressed): wasLeft = state left_to_you && !pressed. The press's card is therefore filed as headMovedNow files it. The merge step's own check in run() passes nothing, so the retry pass and a card's Merge behave as before. compose and both test worlds (chainWorld, the w15-tail restarted world) pass the option on: (task, o) => dependents.checkBeforeMerge(task, o).

tests_changed_for_design.test: packages/runtime/test/dependent-branches-merge.test.ts chainWorld() and the w15-tail restarted() world
tests_changed_for_design.why: Wiring only, so the test worlds match compose: merge.checkBranchesWith((task, o) => dependents.checkBeforeMerge(task, o)) now passes the press's options. No assertion changed.

new_problems: The race 'the watcher's poll rebuilds B between the press's read and its head check' is now handled by headMovedNow's re-read. That path depends on GitHub's PR API showing a force-push at once. If the API lags, the press can still refuse with the head-moved sentence, and the step would refuse it a moment later the same way (this predates the area). Only live check 4 can show whether real GitHub lags there.

Pre-existing in settleRecord, not changed here: the record moves to the rebuilt head before the push. If the push then fails, the record names a head GitHub does not have. The press path is safe, because the check then returns owed and the press is refused or waits. A later merge step would compare GitHub's old head with the moved record.
notes_for_other_areas:
loop/merge.ts:
- New export BranchCheckOptions { pressed?: boolean }.
- BranchCheck is now (task, o?: BranchCheckOptions) => Promise<BranchVerdict>; ReviewedPrMerge.checkBranchNow(task, o = {}) passes o to the check.
- BranchVerdict { left, owed } is unchanged.
- headMovedNow(task, head) keeps its signature. It now reads the pull request again first, and returns null for a fresh head equal to the reviewed commit or a pull request no longer open. Its record, reason and card name the fresh head.

session/dependent-branches.ts: checkBeforeMerge(task, o?: BranchCheckOptions). Private settleRecord(r, pr, pressed = false) and changedAfterReview(task, record, pr, pressed = false): with pressed, the card is filed also over a record that waited for the click. Any new wiring must pass o through, as compose.ts does: merge.checkBranchesWith((task, o) => dependentBranches.checkBeforeMerge(task, o)).

daemon/pull-requests.ts merge(): the press calls checkBranchNow(task, { pressed: true }) and keeps rebuiltNow, the tasks whose record the check moved; the head check skips them. Nothing else in read()/readView changed (C2's docs-rows edits are unaffected).

apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts is unchanged. The route's answer shape is unchanged, and the fake's default press answer ('Merging #N.') already matches the restored behaviour. The new real-daemon case is in the 'l3-merge, run L3' describe.
No new ADR. ADR 0111's 2026-11-15 amendment has an appended fix-up note.

Suggested UPDATE-LOG / CHANGELOG line (session lead): 'Merge pressed on a pull request right after the one it builds on was squash- or rebase-merged on GitHub merges it again, after rebuilding it onto main; it is no longer refused as changed after the review (review of L3-github-1/L3-github-3).'
